evidence.C1: Art shows 'depth in the water' and 'light that changes' (night shot with lanterns), but static shots limit full verification of 'convincing form' in motion.
evidence.C2: Full-screen 'Eye button' mode achieves 'controls are quiet', but the persistent 'Level 1' and coin header in standard view introduces gamification that slightly conflicts with 'ASMR relax'.
evidence.C3: Design matches anchor perfectly: 'rich adjustable soundscape', 'moods', 'sleep timer', and 'gentle, discoverable interactions' like drag-to-lead and name cards.
evidence.C4: Mixer sheet is 'clear and well grouped', but mobile controls switch to icons-only which reduces clarity compared to desktop text labels.

fixes: Ensure the 'Eye' button (calm mode) hides the global app header (Level 1, Coins) to fully achieve the 'nothing jarring' anchor for C2.
Add tooltips or accessible labels to the mobile icon-only control bar (Speaker, Sun, Drop) to match the clarity of the desktop text labels (C4).
Tune the koi schooling algorithm during feeding to prevent tight clustering that risks looking like a 'blob' rather than individual fish with 'convincing form' (C1).

evidence.C1: Koi are recognisable with varied patterns (kohaku, ogon, asagi visible), time-of-day lighting changes work (lanterns glow, moon reflection, fireflies at night), composition is balanced with stones/lily pads/lanterns. However, koi forms look somewhat simplified/cartoonish rather than convincing, and water depth is suggested by caustic patterns but the surface reads as fairly flat.
evidence.C2: Full-screen calm mode (dusk screenshot) looks finished with all UI hidden, bottom control bar is a quiet pill, no jarring elements. But the header tabs, stats line, and the always-visible hint bar 'Tap the water · Hold to feed · Drag to lead · Tap a koi to meet it' keep UI present in normal mode.
evidence.C3: Multiple gentle interactions described (tap ripple, hold feed, drag lead, tap koi for name card, tap leaf to spin), rich soundscape with stream/fountain/wind chimes/crickets/rain/plops/pellet ticks/gulps, positional panning, sounds sheet with volume, layer toggles, mood (Auto/Day/Dusk/Night), koi count 5/9/13, sleep timer 10/20/30 min. Cannot verify actual audio quality.
evidence.C4: Desktop (1440) layout is tidy with clean header tabs and compact bottom control bar. Phone (390) scales well with icon-only controls and bottom tab bar. Sounds sheet is well-grouped into Volume/Layers/Mood/Koi count/Sleep timer sections with clear labels and sliders.

fixes: Make koi forms more convincing — current koi read as simplified/cartoonish shapes; add more body curvature, fin detail, and pattern fidelity so they look like real nishikigoi rather than stylized blobs.
Deepen the water — caustic patterns suggest depth but the surface looks flat; add subtle gradient, underwater shadowing, or layered translucency so the pond reads as having real volume.

Auto-hide or fade the persistent hint bar ('Tap the water · Hold to feed · Drag to lead · Tap a koi to meet it') after first interaction so the normal view feels calmer and closer to the full-screen calm mode.

evidence.C1: Pleasant coherent pond: caustics, depth gradient, mossy stone rim, 'lantern glow, moon reflection, fireflies' at night show time-of-day light; but koi read as flat patterned cutouts (yellow ogon reads leaf-like at a glance), short of 'convincing form and colour'.
evidence.C2: 'Eye button: calm full-screen mode with all UI hidden' and the dusk calm shot looks finished; night shot hides controls. But desktop tab keeps nav pill, heading, description and stats line ('Just arrived · 0 pellets eaten') above the scene, and the hint pill sits over the water.
evidence.C3: 'tap water for a ripple... hold to feed, drag to lead koi, tap a koi for its name card', keys, plus 'volume, layer toggles, mood, koi count 5/9/13, sleep timer 10/20/30 min that fades out and dims' and position panning — full 10-anchor checklist on paper; only leaf-spin is shallow and undiscoverable.
evidence.C4: Mixer sheet is clear and well grouped (Volume / Layers with % / Mood / Koi in the pond / Sleep timer); tidy at 1440 and 390, but the phone control row drops to icon-only circles, losing the labels shown on desktop.

fixes: C1 (w=0.35, biggest lever): make koi read as fish, not stickers — add head/eye definition, volumetric body shading and better fin/tail articulation, and vary idle spacing so the school isn't always centre-clustered.

C2 (w=0.25): let the scene dominate the desktop tab — condense the heading/description/stats block, auto-dismiss the hint pill after first interaction, and fade the bottom control bar when idle in every mood (night shot already does this).
C4 (w=0.20): restore labels or add first-run tooltips for the 390px icon-only control row, and ensure the Sounds sheet signals scroll so the Sleep timer row isn't apparently cut off.
